name: James Cleverly
role: British Conservative MP; former home secretary and foreign secretary
summary: Cleverly advocates deregulation, private investment, smaller government and reduced immigration. His record combines support for international alliances and nuclear deterrence with environmental action, nuclear energy, and legal abortion and same-sex marriage.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He argues for private enterprise over ministerial allocation of investment.

public-ownership.rationale: He explicitly rejects creating state-owned companies to lower costs.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He advocates deregulation rather than solving problems through additional business regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: He calls welfare spending excessive, rejects dependency as a way of life and advocates getting recipients into work.

empower-police-military.rationale: He personally advocates expanded police authority to prevent disruptive protest offences.

decide-locally.rationale: He names local empowerment and local consent as foundations for environmental policymaking.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: His own blog supports gay marriage and rejects claims that it harms heterosexual marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: His written parliamentary answer explicitly supports access to safe and legal abortion.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He explicitly seeks lower migration and defends his own restrictions on salaries and dependants.

free-trade.rationale: He explicitly says freer trade benefits small businesses, women and prosperity.

limit-growth.rationale: He explicitly rejects degrowth and favors simultaneous economic expansion and emissions reductions.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He demands urgent climate action, endorsing net-zero commitments and major international climate finance.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He calls for overcoming planning barriers to nuclear projects and deploying small modular reactors.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He opposes taxing entrepreneurs so ministers and civil servants can allocate their capital.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Asked about the monarchy’s role, he says its inherited structure works and welcomes its international connections.

democracy-best.rationale: He praises democratic accountability as a national strength and advocates defending democracy internationally.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He rejects powerful countries invading weaker neighbors and defends sovereign territorial integrity.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He explicitly supports preserving Israel’s Jewish democratic identity alongside Palestinian statehood.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He expressly affirms universal rights to dignity and freedom from torture, slavery and arbitrary detention.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He advocates reinforced NATO and transatlantic cooperation, rejecting isolationism.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He says vulnerable island states deserve support and calls on international powers to share climate burdens.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: He explicitly supports retaining Britain’s own nuclear deterrent as the ultimate security guarantee.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: He advocates negotiated borders based on 1967 lines with agreed land swaps.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: He rejects unilateral West Bank annexation as unlawful, insisting borders require agreement.

corporate-influence.rationale: He criticizes lobbyists seeking subsidies and regulation to protect shareholders from risk.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: He proposes recognizing children in taxation and reducing childcare costs to enable larger families instead of migration-driven growth.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Despite supporting restrictions on disruptive offences, he explicitly calls the right to protest paramount.

assisted-dying.rationale: He opposed the 2025 bill over coercion, clinical capacity and safeguards, expressly distinguishing its details from the general principle.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He explicitly supports close US and European defense cooperation against shared threats.

future-generations.rationale: He endorses environmental guardianship for future generations as a duty.

arms-reduction.rationale: He advocates minimum credible nuclear capability and negotiated conventional arms control, while permitting a higher warhead ceiling.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He explicitly advocates international financial reform addressing developing countries’ particular needs.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: He advocates retention while pursuing eventual multilateral disarmament rather than unilateral abandonment.

no-business-privileges.rationale: He rejects government subsidies that transfer business risks onto taxpayers.

notes: No inference from party affiliation or government membership. Own statements span pre-parliamentary writing, foreign and home secretary service, leadership campaign and subsequent assisted-dying debate. The 2025 assisted-dying speech opposes specific safeguards and implementation; it is not the later Diane Abbott passage supporting the principle. His China engagement does not mean preferring China to the United States. Removal to Rwanda does not establish expulsion of an ethnic minority. The downloaded full texts and remaining null statements were checked across themes. Generic equality does not establish specific transgender laws, religious policies or women’s institutions; budget restraint alone does not establish opposition to deficit stimulus or legally binding fiscal rules. Technology optimism about clean energy does not establish a belief that technology solves most human problems.
